newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares seek direction after recent highs.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares seek direction after recent highs.

text.p: Belgian shares are seen seeking direction next week after closing flat Friday on the heels of Thursday's record high Bel-20 close.
"We need confirmation that yesterday's breaking of resistance levels will hold," said a dealer.
The Bel-20 index .BFX ended flat, down 0.77 point to 1,773.21 points.
Bank shares closed down following news that banks are to pay 0.06 percent tax on amounts outstanding in savings book accounts as part of the 1997 budget austerity effort.

"There's about 3,000 billion francs outstanding in savings book accounts," said Bank Degroof analyst Jan Longeval. "At a 0.06 percent rate, that means the tax will cost the bank sector as a whole about 1.8 billion francs," Longeval said. This total cost is pre-tax for the banks.
Generale Bank and Kredietbank were down two and 0.5 percent, to 10,925 and 10,275 francs per share respectively, on news of the budget tax plan.
Banque Bruxelles Lambert went against the trend, closing up 20 francs to 6,130 francs per share.
